classification.difficultyReason: Calculate quarter and three-quarter positions from each total, identify the discrete scores whose cumulative bars contain those positions and subtract to obtain IQR.

content.prompt: Determine the IQR for these cumulative histograms.

spec.description: Six adjacent outlined cumulative-frequency bars centred on weights 20 through 25, with horizontal grid lines, labelled axes and numeric ticks. Decorative violet fill is omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied histogram is visible; quartiles and IQR belong to editable answers.

answer.worked:
Total frequency: $60$.
$$\begin{aligned}Q_1\text{ position}&=0.25\times60=15\\Q_3\text{ position}&=0.75\times60=45\end{aligned}$$
The cumulative histogram gives $Q_1=22\text{ kg}$ and $Q_3=23\text{ kg}$.
$$\mathrm{IQR}=23-22=1\text{ kg}.$$

spec.description: Seven adjacent outlined cumulative-frequency bars centred on defect counts 0 through 6, with horizontal grid lines, labelled axes and numeric ticks. Decorative violet fill is omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied histogram is visible; quartiles and IQR belong to editable answers.

answer.worked:
Total frequency: $50$.
$$\begin{aligned}Q_1\text{ position}&=0.25\times50=12.5\\Q_3\text{ position}&=0.75\times50=37.5\end{aligned}$$
The cumulative histogram gives $Q_1=1$ defect and $Q_3=5$ defects.
$$\mathrm{IQR}=5-1=4\text{ defects}.$$
